mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 4.5%) signals an accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.2 percentage points in one month) signals deteriorating labor market conditions and economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS show positive growth, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) during early-cycle expansion signals improving manufacturing output and economic growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising and the economy is in early-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth is above 2.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflationary pressures that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth is above 100k and UNRATE is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly job growth (PAYEMS) during periods of labor market tightness (low unemployment) signals sustained economic momentum, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth is above 100k and UNRATE is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.
